GeometryNodeInputIndex.node: Gives every element (point, face, and so on) its position number in the list, starting at 0. Use it to treat elements differently, like every second one.

GeometryNodeInputInstanceBounds.node: Finds the smallest box around each instance's geometry and gives its corners. Use it to know how big each instance is.

inputs.Use Radius: When on, point and curve radius count toward the box size. When off, only the raw point positions are used.

GeometryNodeInputInstanceReference.node: Gives the number of the instance reference each instance uses. Handy for telling which kind of object each instance is.

GeometryNodeInputInstanceRotation.node: Gives the rotation of each instance as a value you can read or change with fields. Use it to see how each copy is turned.

GeometryNodeInputInstanceScale.node: Gives the size of each instance as a vector (X, Y, Z). Use it to read how big or small each copy is.

GeometryNodeInputMaterial.node: Outputs one material you pick in the node. Plug it into Set Material or Replace Material to use that material.

GeometryNodeInputMaterialIndex.node: Gives which material slot number each face or element uses. Use it to find or sort parts by material.

GeometryNodeInputMeshEdgeAngle.node: Gives the angle between the two faces touching each edge. Flat edges give a low value, sharp corners give a high one. Good for finding sharp edges.

GeometryNodeInputMeshEdgeNeighbors.node: Counts how many faces touch each edge. Normal closed shapes give 2, open border edges give 1. Use it to find holes and borders.

GeometryNodeInputMeshEdgeVertices.node: Gives the two vertex numbers at the ends of each edge, plus their positions. Use it to find where an edge starts and ends.

GeometryNodeInputMeshFaceArea.node: Gives the surface size of each face. Big faces give big numbers. Use it to treat large and small faces differently.

GeometryNodeInputMeshFaceIsPlanar.node: Tells if each face is flat (true) or bent (false). Use it to find faces that are warped.

inputs.Threshold: How much bending still counts as flat. Low is strict, only perfectly flat faces pass. High allows slightly bent faces.

GeometryNodeInputMeshFaceNeighbors.node: Gives how many faces and vertices each face has around it. Use it to tell triangles, quads and bigger faces apart.

GeometryNodeInputMeshIsland.node: Finds separate pieces of a mesh that are not connected to each other. Gives each piece a number and the total count of pieces.

GeometryNodeInputMeshVertexNeighbors.node: Gives how many edges and faces touch each vertex. Use it to find crowded corners or isolated points.

GeometryNodeInputNamedAttribute.node: Reads a saved attribute by its name and gives you the values. Use it to get data stored earlier or painted in the mesh.

inputs.Name: The exact name of the attribute to read. Names must match exactly, including capital letters.

GeometryNodeInputNamedLayerSelection.node: Gives true for the Grease Pencil layer you name, and false for the others. Use it to pick one drawing layer.

inputs.Name: The name of the Grease Pencil layer to select. It must match the layer name exactly.

GeometryNodeInputNormal.node: Gives the direction each face or vertex points away from the surface, like an arrow sticking out. Use it to push or align things outward.

GeometryNodeInputObject.node: Outputs one object you pick in the node. Plug it into Object Info or other nodes that need an object.

GeometryNodeInputPosition.node: Gives the location of each point in 3D space as X, Y, Z. Use it to base changes on where something is.

GeometryNodeInputRadius.node: Gives the thickness of each curve point or point cloud point. Use it to read or reuse the sizes already set.

GeometryNodeInputSceneTime.node: Gives the current time of the animation in seconds and in frames. Use it to animate things as the timeline plays.

GeometryNodeInputShadeSmooth.node: Tells if each face is set to smooth shading (true) or flat shading (false). Use it to find which faces look smooth.

GeometryNodeInputShortestEdgePaths.node: For each vertex, finds the next step on the shortest route along edges to the nearest end vertex. Use it to make paths like rivers or cracks.

inputs.End Vertex: Marks which vertices are the goals where paths end. Every path runs toward the closest marked vertex.
inputs.Edge Cost: How hard it is to travel along each edge. Low means easy, paths prefer it. High means costly, paths avoid it.

GeometryNodeInputSplineCyclic.node: Tells if each curve closes into a loop (true) or has open ends (false). Use it to find the closed curves.

GeometryNodeInputSplineResolution.node: Gives how many points each curve gets when it is drawn. Higher numbers mean smoother curves.

GeometryNodeInputTangent.node: Gives the direction a curve is heading at each point, like which way a train faces on a track. Use it to align things along a curve.

GeometryNodeInputVoxelIndex.node: Gives the whole-number X, Y, Z address of the voxel (a 3D pixel) being checked. Use it to tell voxels apart inside a volume grid.

GeometryNodeInstanceOnPoints.node: Places a copy of some geometry on every point. Copies are cheap instances. Use it to scatter trees, rocks or bolts.

inputs.Selection: Picks which points get a copy. True places an instance there, false leaves the point empty.
inputs.Pick Instance: When on, each point picks one item from the instances you give it. When off, all items are placed together at every point.
inputs.Instance Index: Chooses which item to use at each point when Pick Instance is on. 0 is the first, 1 the second, and so on.
inputs.Rotation: Turns each copy. Zero keeps it straight. Plug in a random value or a normal-based rotation for variety.
inputs.Scale: Sizes each copy. 1 is original size, lower is smaller, higher is bigger. Different X, Y, Z values stretch it.

GeometryNodeInstanceTransform.node: Gives the full position, rotation and size of each instance packed into one matrix. Use it to copy or reuse an instance's placement.

GeometryNodeInstancesToPoints.node: Turns each instance into a single point at its center. Use it when you want to work with where the copies are, not what they look like.

inputs.Selection: Picks which instances become points. True means converted, false means skipped.
inputs.Position: Where each new point is placed. By default it uses the instance's own origin, so you rarely change this.
inputs.Radius: The size of each created point. Low is tiny dots, high is big dots. Only matters for display and some later nodes.

GeometryNodeInterpolateCurves.node: Makes new hair-like curves by blending between existing guide curves. Use it to fill a hairy area from a few guide strands.

inputs.Guide Up: The up direction of the guide curves. It helps new curves bend the same way as their guides.
inputs.Guide Group ID: Sorts guide curves into groups. New curves only blend with guides that share their group number.
inputs.Point Up: The up direction at each new point's start. It keeps the new curves facing the right way.
inputs.Point Group ID: Group number of each new point. It only uses guides that have the same group number.
inputs.Max Neighbors: How many nearby guide curves are blended. Low (1) copies one guide exactly. High mixes many for a smoother, softer result.

GeometryNodeIsViewport.node: Tells if the nodes are running for the 3D viewport (true) or for a final render (false). Use it to keep the viewport light and render detailed.

GeometryNodeJoinGeometry.node: Glues many separate geometries into one. Use it to combine a mesh, curves and points so they travel as a single piece.

GeometryNodeListGetItem.node: Picks one value out of a list by its position number. Use it to grab, for example, the third item.

inputs.List: The list of values you want to pick from.
inputs.Index: The position of the item to take. 0 is the first item. Too high a number gives a default empty value.

GeometryNodeListLength.node: Counts how many items are in a list. Use it to know the size of a list before looping or picking items.

inputs.List: The list to count. Its number of items is returned.

GeometryNodeMaterialSelection.node: Gives true for faces that use the chosen material and false for the rest. Use it to change only the parts with that material.

inputs.Material: The material to look for. Faces using it are selected.

GeometryNodeMenuSwitch.node: Lets you choose one of several named inputs from a drop-down menu. Use it to switch between versions of a setup.

inputs.Menu: Picks which named option is passed through. You can plug in a value to choose it from outside the node.

GeometryNodeMergeByDistance.node: Joins points or vertices that are close together into one. Use it to clean up doubled points left after combining meshes.

inputs.Selection: Picks which points can be merged. Unselected points stay as they are.
inputs.Mode: All merges any points within the distance. Connected only merges points that already share an edge.
inputs.Distance: How close points must be to merge. Zero merges only overlapping points. Higher values merge points that are further apart.

GeometryNodeMergeLayers.node: Joins groups of Grease Pencil layers into single layers. Use it to simplify a drawing with many layers.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Group ID: Layers with the same number are merged into one layer. Different numbers stay separate.

GeometryNodeMergePoints.node: Merges points that share the same ID number into one. Use it to weld chosen points together, even if they are far apart.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Merge ID: Points with the same number are merged together. Points with different numbers stay apart.

GeometryNodeMeshBevel.node: Rounds or cuts off sharp edges or corners so they catch light nicely. Use it to make shapes look less razor sharp.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Affect Kind: Chooses whether edges or vertices get bevelled. Edges rounds the sides, vertices rounds the corners.
inputs.Start Left Offset: How far the bevel reaches on the left side at the start of each edge. Zero means none, higher cuts deeper.
inputs.Start Right Offset: How far the bevel reaches on the right side at the start of each edge. Zero means none, higher cuts deeper.
inputs.End Left Offset: How far the bevel reaches on the left side at the end of each edge. Zero means none, higher cuts deeper.
inputs.End Right Offset: How far the bevel reaches on the right side at the end of each edge. Zero means none, higher cuts deeper.
inputs.Offset: How wide the bevel is. Low gives a tiny rounded edge. High gives a big chamfer that eats into the shape.
inputs.Miter: When on, bevels meeting at a corner end in sharp points instead of rounding over.
inputs.Spread: How far a mitered corner extends. Low keeps the corner tight, high spreads it wider.
inputs.Segments: How many slices make up the bevel. 1 is a flat cut, higher numbers make it smoother and rounder.
inputs.Shape: Curve of the bevel profile. Low looks flat or concave, 0.5 is round, high looks bulging or squarish.

GeometryNodeMeshBoolean.node: Cuts, subtracts or joins meshes using solid-shape logic. Use it to carve holes in a mesh or merge solid shapes together.

inputs.Self Intersection: When on, parts of the same mesh that cross each other are also handled. Slower but safer for messy meshes.
inputs.Hole Tolerant: When on, tries to work even if the mesh has holes. It is slower, so turn it on only if results look wrong.

GeometryNodeMeshCircle.node: Makes a ring of vertices joined by edges, like a hoop. Use it as a profile for pipes or as a base for curves.

inputs.Vertices: How many points the ring has. Low like 3 gives a triangle, high like 64 looks like a smooth circle.
inputs.Radius: How far the ring is from its center. Small is a tight ring, large is a wide ring.

GeometryNodeMeshCone.node: Makes a cone or a cut-off cone shape. Use it for spikes, funnels, cups or trees.

inputs.Vertices: How many points around the circle base. Low looks chunky and faceted, high looks smooth and round.
inputs.Side Segments: How many rings of faces go up the side. More gives more detail for bending or bumps.
inputs.Fill Segments: How many rings of faces fill the top and bottom caps. 1 is a plain flat cap.
inputs.Radius Top: Width of the top. 0 makes a sharp point. The same as the bottom makes a cylinder.
inputs.Radius Bottom: Width of the bottom. Small gives a thin cone, large gives a wide base.
inputs.Depth: The height of the cone. Small is flat and squat, large is tall and thin.

GeometryNodeMeshCube.node: Makes a box with any size on each side. Use it as a quick block, wall, floor or building piece.

inputs.Size: Length of the box on X, Y and Z. Small numbers make a tiny box, big numbers make a huge one.
inputs.Vertices X: How many points along the X side. 2 is just the corners, more adds cuts for bending or detail.
inputs.Vertices Y: How many points along the Y side. 2 is just the corners, more adds cuts for bending or detail.
inputs.Vertices Z: How many points along the Z side. 2 is just the corners, more adds cuts for bending or detail.

GeometryNodeMeshCylinder.node: Makes a tube shape with flat ends. Use it for pipes, columns, cans or wheels.

inputs.Vertices: How many points around the circle. Low looks like a prism with flat sides, high looks round and smooth.
inputs.Side Segments: How many rings of faces go along the side. More gives more detail for bending.
inputs.Fill Segments: How many rings of faces fill each end cap. 1 is a plain flat cap.
inputs.Radius: How wide the cylinder is. Small is thin like a pencil, large is wide like a barrel.
inputs.Depth: How tall the cylinder is. Small is flat like a coin, large is long like a pole.

GeometryNodeMeshFaceSetBoundaries.node: Finds edges that sit between faces with different group numbers. Use it to outline regions, like borders on a map.

inputs.Face Set: The group number of each face. Edges where the number changes are selected.

GeometryNodeMeshGrid.node: Makes a flat sheet of squares lying on the ground (X and Y). Use it for floors, terrain or cloth.

inputs.Size X: Width of the grid along X. Small is a tiny patch, large is a wide field.
inputs.Size Y: Length of the grid along Y. Small is a tiny patch, large is a long field.
inputs.Vertices X: How many points along X. Low gives big squares, high gives fine detail for bending or displacing.
inputs.Vertices Y: How many points along Y. Low gives big squares, high gives fine detail for bending or displacing.

GeometryNodeMeshIcoSphere.node: Makes a ball built from equal triangles. Use it when you want a sphere without squeezed spots at the poles.

inputs.Radius: Distance from the center to the surface. Small is marble-sized, large is planet-sized.
inputs.Subdivisions: How many times the triangles are split. 1 is a rough shape, higher is smoother but heavier. Very high values get slow.

GeometryNodeMeshLine.node: Makes a row of points joined by edges. Use it as a path, a base for curves or a line of copies.

inputs.Count: How many points are in the line. Low gives a short chain, high gives a dense line.
inputs.Resolution: The spacing between points when using length mode. Small packs them close, large spreads them out.
inputs.Start Location: Where the first point sits in 3D space. Change it to move the whole line.
inputs.Offset: The step from one point to the next as X, Y, Z. It sets the direction and spacing of the line.

GeometryNodeMeshToCurve.node: Turns mesh edges into curves. Use it to make pipes, wires or paths from a mesh outline.

inputs.Selection: Picks which edges become curves. True means used, false means skipped.

GeometryNodeMeshToDensityGrid.node: Fills the inside of a mesh with a volume grid of density numbers. Use it for clouds or smoke shaped like a mesh.

inputs.Density: How thick the volume is inside the mesh. Low is thin like mist, high is thick and dark.
inputs.Voxel Size: Size of each tiny 3D cell. Small gives sharp detail but is slow and heavy. Large is fast but blocky.
inputs.Gradient Width: How soft the edge is where the volume fades out. Low is a hard edge, high is a soft fuzzy fade.

GeometryNodeMeshToPoints.node: Turns mesh vertices (or other parts) into a cloud of points. Use it to scatter things on a mesh or show only the dots.

inputs.Selection: Picks which vertices become points. True means used, false means skipped.
inputs.Position: Where each point goes. By default it keeps the original vertex position.
inputs.Radius: Size of each point. Low is tiny dots, high is big dots. It matters for display and later nodes.

GeometryNodeMeshToSDFGrid.node: Turns a mesh into a signed distance field, a 3D grid that stores how far each spot is from the surface. Use it to smooth or merge shapes.

inputs.Voxel Size: Size of each 3D cell in the grid. Small gives fine detail but is slow. Large is fast but rough.
inputs.Band Width: How many cells around the surface are stored. Low is fast but limits later effects. High gives more room to work.

GeometryNodeMeshToVolume.node: Turns a mesh into a fog volume that looks like its surface. Use it for clouds, smoke or glowing shapes.

inputs.Density: How thick the fog is. Low is faint mist, high is dense and dark.
inputs.Resolution Mode: Choose Amount to set how many cells fit the object, or Size to set the exact cell size.
inputs.Voxel Size: Size of each 3D cell when using Size mode. Small means fine detail but heavy. Large means fast but blocky.
inputs.Voxel Amount: How many cells span the object when using Amount mode. Low is coarse and fast, high is detailed and slow.
inputs.Interior Band Width: How deep the fog goes inside the surface. Low makes a thin shell, high fills the shape further.

GeometryNodeMeshUVSphere.node: Makes a ball from rings and segments, like a globe with lines of latitude and longitude. Use it for planets, eyes or balls.

inputs.Segments: How many slices around the ball, like orange wedges. Low looks faceted, high looks smooth.
inputs.Rings: How many horizontal bands from top to bottom. Low looks chunky, high looks round.
inputs.Radius: Distance from center to surface. Small is marble-sized, large is planet-sized.

GeometryNodeObjectInfo.node: Reads info from another object, such as its position, rotation, size and shape. Use it to bring another object into your node setup.

inputs.Object: The object to read from. Pick one from your scene.
inputs.As Instance: Off copies the real geometry. On brings it as a light instance, which is faster and can be placed many times.

GeometryNodeOffsetCornerInFace.node: Finds a neighbouring corner in the same face, a set number of steps away. Use it to look at the next or previous corner of a face.

inputs.Corner Index: The starting corner. By default it is each corner itself.
inputs.Offset: How many corners to step around the face. Positive goes forward, negative goes backward, 0 stays put.

GeometryNodeOffsetPointInCurve.node: Finds a point a set number of steps along the same curve. Use it to look at the next or previous point on a curve.

inputs.Point Index: The starting point. By default it is each point itself.
inputs.Offset: How many points to step along the curve. Positive goes forward, negative goes backward, 0 stays put.

GeometryNodePoints.node: Makes a cloud of loose points, each with its own position and size. Use it to build a starting set of dots to instance on.

inputs.Count: How many points to make. Low gives just a few, high gives a dense cloud.
inputs.Position: Where each point is placed in 3D space. Plug in a field such as random values to spread them out.
inputs.Radius: Size of each point. Low is tiny dots, high is large dots.

GeometryNodePointsOfCurve.node: Finds a point index that belongs to a chosen curve. Use it to pick, for example, the first or last point of each curve.

inputs.Curve Index: Which curve to look in. By default it is each curve's own number.
inputs.Weights: Numbers used to sort the points. Lower values come first in the order.
inputs.Sort Index: Which spot in the sorted order to take. 0 is the first point, 1 the second, and so on.

GeometryNodePointsToCurves.node: Joins points into curves. Points sharing a group number become one curve, ordered by weight. Use it to draw lines through points.

inputs.Curve Group ID: Points with the same number end up in the same curve. Different numbers make different curves.
inputs.Weight: Sets the order of points along each curve. Lower weights come first, higher weights come later.

GeometryNodePointsToSDFGrid.node: Turns points into a signed distance field made of little spheres. Use it to blob points together into a smooth shape.

inputs.Radius: Size of the sphere around each point. Small gives separate blobs, large makes them overlap and merge.
inputs.Voxel Size: Size of each 3D cell. Small gives fine detail but is slow. Large is fast but rough.

GeometryNodePointsToVertices.node: Turns each point in a point cloud into a mesh vertex. Use it to get real mesh dots you can connect or edit.

inputs.Selection: Picks which points become mesh vertices. True means used, false means skipped.

GeometryNodePointsToVolume.node: Puts a ball of fog around every point. Use it for clouds, sparks or glowing particles.

inputs.Density: How thick the fog is. Low is faint mist, high is dense and dark.
inputs.Resolution Mode: Choose Amount to set how many cells fit the object, or Size to set the exact cell size.
inputs.Voxel Size: Size of each 3D cell when using Size mode. Small means fine detail but heavy. Large means fast but blocky.
inputs.Voxel Amount: How many cells span the object when using Amount mode. Low is coarse and fast, high is detailed and slow.
inputs.Radius: Size of the fog ball at each point. Small gives little puffs, large gives big clouds that overlap.

GeometryNodeProximity.node: Finds the closest spot on another shape for each element. Gives that position and the distance. Use it to react to nearby objects.

inputs.Group ID: Splits the target into groups. Only target parts with the matching number are searched.
inputs.Source Position: The spot to measure from. By default it is each element's own position.
inputs.Sample Group ID: Group number of the element that is searching. It matches against the target's Group ID.

GeometryNodeRaycast.node: Shoots invisible rays and finds where they hit another shape. Use it to drop things onto a surface or check for walls.

inputs.Attribute: The value to read from the surface where the ray hits, like a color or number.
inputs.Interpolation: How the value is read at the hit spot. Interpolated blends nearby values smoothly, Nearest takes the closest one.
inputs.Source Position: Where each ray starts. Move it to shoot from different spots.
inputs.Ray Direction: Which way the ray points. (0, 0, -1) shoots straight down.
inputs.Ray Length: How far the ray can travel. Short rays only find nearby things, long rays reach far.

GeometryNodeRealizeInstances.node: Turns light instances into real geometry you can edit point by point. Use it when you need to change or join the copies.

inputs.Selection: Picks which instances are turned into real geometry. The rest stay as instances.
inputs.Realize All: On realizes every level of nested instances. Off lets you choose how deep with Depth.
inputs.Depth: How many layers of nested instances to make real. 1 only goes one level, higher goes deeper.

GeometryNodeRemoveAttribute.node: Deletes attributes from the geometry by name. Use it to clean up data you no longer need and make things lighter.

inputs.Pattern Mode: Exact removes only the attribute with that name. Wildcard lets you use * to match many names at once.
inputs.Name: The attribute name to delete. In wildcard mode, * matches any text.

GeometryNodeRenameAttribute.node: Changes the name of an attribute. Use it to match names used by other nodes or materials.

inputs.Mode: Exact renames one attribute. Wildcard renames many whose names match a pattern.
inputs.Old: The current name of the attribute you want to change.
inputs.New: The new name to give it.
inputs.Overwrite: When on, an attribute that already has the new name is replaced. When off, nothing is replaced.

GeometryNodeRepeatInput.node: Starts a repeat zone that runs the nodes inside it again and again. Use it to build things step by step, like growing a pattern.

inputs.Iterations: How many times the zone runs. 0 skips it, 1 runs once, larger numbers repeat more but get slower.

GeometryNodeRepeatOutput.node: Ends a repeat zone and sends out the result after the last loop. What you plug in here feeds back into the next loop.

GeometryNodeReplaceMaterial.node: Swaps one material for another on the geometry. Use it to recolor or restyle parts without editing the mesh.

inputs.Old: The material to look for and replace.
inputs.New: The material to use in its place.

GeometryNodeResampleCurve.node: Rebuilds curves with new evenly spaced points, as straight pieces. Use it to simplify or even out a curve.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Mode: Count makes a set number of points. Length places points a set distance apart. Evaluated keeps the curve's own points.
inputs.Count: How many points each curve gets in Count mode. Low is rough and angular, high is smooth.
inputs.Length: The gap between points in Length mode. Small gives many close points, large gives few spread points.

GeometryNodeReverseCurve.node: Flips the direction of curves so the end becomes the start. Use it when something runs the wrong way along the curve.

inputs.Selection: Picks which curves get flipped. True means reversed, false means left as is.

GeometryNodeRotateInstances.node: Turns instances around, in their own space or the world. Use it to spin or tilt each copy differently.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Rotation: How much to turn each instance. Zero changes nothing. Bigger angles turn them more.
inputs.Pivot Point: The center they spin around. By default it is each instance's own origin.
inputs.Local Space: On rotates each instance around its own axes. Off rotates around the world axes.

GeometryNodeSDFGridBoolean.node: Combines signed distance field grids by union, intersect or difference. Use it to merge or carve smooth volume shapes.

inputs.Grid 1: The first grid used in the operation.
inputs.Grid 2: The second grid used in the operation.

GeometryNodeSDFGridFillet.node: Rounds off inner corners of a signed distance field surface. Use it to soften sharp creases where shapes meet.

inputs.Grid: The signed distance grid to round off.
inputs.Iterations: How many times the rounding repeats. Low is subtle, high rounds more but takes longer.

GeometryNodeSDFGridLaplacian.node: Smooths a signed distance field using Laplacian flow. Use it to even out bumps and noise on a volume surface.

inputs.Grid: The signed distance grid to smooth.
inputs.Iterations: How many smoothing passes run. Low is slight, high is very smooth and may shrink details.

GeometryNodeSDFGridMean.node: Smooths a signed distance field by averaging nearby values (box filter). Fast way to soften a volume shape.

inputs.Grid: The signed distance grid to smooth.
inputs.Width: How far around each cell is averaged. Low is a light blur, high is a heavy blur.
inputs.Iterations: How many times the filter repeats. Low is subtle, high is very smooth.

GeometryNodeSDFGridMeanCurvature.node: Smooths a signed distance field by flattening curved bumps (mean curvature flow). Use it to round surfaces evenly.

inputs.Grid: The signed distance grid to smooth.
inputs.Iterations: How many smoothing passes run. Low is slight, high shrinks and rounds the shape more.

GeometryNodeSDFGridMedian.node: Smooths a signed distance field with a median filter, picking the middle value nearby. Removes noise but keeps edges fairly sharp.

inputs.Grid: The signed distance grid to clean up.
inputs.Width: How far around each cell is checked. Low touches only tiny noise, high changes more.
inputs.Iterations: How many times the filter repeats. Low is subtle, high cleans more.

GeometryNodeSDFGridOffset.node: Pushes the surface of a signed distance field outward or inward. Use it to make a volume shape fatter or thinner.

inputs.Grid: The signed distance grid to grow or shrink.
inputs.Distance: How far to move the surface. Positive grows it, negative shrinks it, 0 changes nothing.

GeometryNodeSampleCurve.node: Reads a value at a chosen spot along a curve, by length or by factor. Use it to find the position or direction partway along a path.

inputs.Value: The data to read from the curve at the chosen spot, like its position or radius.
inputs.Factor: How far along the curve, from 0 (start) to 1 (end). 0.5 is the middle.
inputs.Length: How far along the curve in distance units. 0 is the start, the curve's total length is the end.
inputs.Curve Index: Which curve to sample when there are several. 0 is the first curve.

GeometryNodeSampleGrid.node: Reads the value of a volume grid at any position in space. Use it to see how dense or far from the surface a spot is.

inputs.Grid: The volume grid to read from.
inputs.Position: The spot in space to read. Change it to sample different places.
inputs.Interpolation: How values between cells are read. Nearest takes the closest cell, higher options blend smoothly.

GeometryNodeSampleGridIndex.node: Reads volume grid values at exact voxel addresses. Use it when you know which cell you want.

inputs.Grid: The volume grid to read from.
inputs.X: The cell number along X. Counts in whole steps from the grid origin.
inputs.Y: The cell number along Y. Counts in whole steps from the grid origin.
inputs.Z: The cell number along Z. Counts in whole steps from the grid origin.

GeometryNodeSampleIndex.node: Reads a value from one chosen element by its index number. Use it to copy data from a specific point, face or edge.

inputs.Value: The data to read from the chosen element.
inputs.Index: The number of the element to read from. 0 is the first one.

GeometryNodeSampleNearest.node: Finds the index of the closest element (point, edge, face) to a position. Use it with Sample Index to copy data from the nearest one.

inputs.Sample Position: The spot to search from. By default it is each element's own position.

GeometryNodeSampleNearestSurface.node: Reads a value from the closest spot on a mesh surface, blending between nearby values. Use it to copy colors or data between meshes.

inputs.Value: The data to read from the mesh surface.
inputs.Group ID: Splits the target mesh into groups. Only parts with the matching number are used.
inputs.Sample Position: The spot to search from. By default it is each element's own position.
inputs.Sample Group ID: The group number of the searching element. It matches the target's Group ID.

GeometryNodeSampleSoundFrequencies.node: Reads how loud a sound is in a range of pitches at a given time. Use it to drive visuals from music.

inputs.Sound: The sound file to listen to.
inputs.Time: The moment in the sound to check, in seconds.
inputs.All Channels: When on, mixes all audio channels (like left and right). When off, uses just one.
inputs.Channel: Which single audio channel to read when All Channels is off. 0 is the first.
inputs.Low: The lowest pitch (in Hz) to measure. Low numbers include deep bass.
inputs.High: The highest pitch (in Hz) to measure. High numbers include treble sounds.
inputs.FFT Size: How finely the sound is split into pitches. Larger gives more precise pitches but less precise timing.
inputs.Window Function: How the slice of sound is shaped before analysis. It changes how clean the result is. Hann is a common choice.

GeometryNodeSampleUVSurface.node: Reads a mesh value at a spot you give on its UV map. Use it to pick up colors or data using texture coordinates.

inputs.Value: The data to read from the mesh at the UV spot.
inputs.Source UV Map: The UV coordinates of the mesh, which tell where each part sits on the flat texture.
inputs.Sample UV: The flat 2D spot to look up. (0, 0) is the bottom left of the UV square, (1, 1) is the top right.

GeometryNodeScaleElements.node: Grows or shrinks connected faces or edges around their own centers. Use it to shrink faces for gaps or inset panels.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Scale: How much to resize. 1 keeps the size, below 1 shrinks, above 1 grows, 0 squeezes to the center.
inputs.Center: The point things scale from, when set manually. By default it is the center of each group.
inputs.Scale Mode: Uniform scales evenly in all directions. Single Axis scales only along the chosen axis.
inputs.Axis: The direction used in Single Axis mode. Only stretching along this line happens.

GeometryNodeScaleInstances.node: Resizes instances, in their own space or the world. Use it to make each copy bigger or smaller.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Scale: The size factor on X, Y, Z. 1 keeps the size, below 1 shrinks, above 1 grows.
inputs.Center: The point instances scale from. By default it is each instance's own origin.
inputs.Local Space: On scales along each instance's own axes. Off scales along the world axes.

GeometryNodeSelfObject.node: Gives the object that this Geometry Nodes modifier is on. Use it to read the object's own position or settings.

GeometryNodeSeparateComponents.node: Splits geometry into its types: mesh, curves, point cloud, volume, instances and more. Use it to handle each type separately.

GeometryNodeSeparateGeometry.node: Splits geometry in two: the selected part and the leftover part. Use it to keep one part and deal with the rest differently.

inputs.Selection: True parts go to the Selection output, false parts go to the Inverted output.

GeometryNodeSetCurveHandlePositions.node: Moves the handles of Bézier curve points to shape the curve. Use it to change how smooth or sharp each bend is.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Position: The new location of the handle in space. Leave it alone to keep the current handle.
inputs.Offset: Moves the handle by this extra amount from where it is. Zero keeps it, bigger values push it away.

GeometryNodeSetCurveNormal.node: Chooses how the sideways (normal) direction of curves is worked out. Use it to control how shapes twist when spread along a curve.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Mode: Minimum Twist keeps it from spinning. Z Up keeps it pointing up. Free uses a normal you give.
inputs.Normal: The direction to use in Free mode. It decides which way the curve's sides face.

GeometryNodeSetCurveRadius.node: Sets the thickness at each curve point. Use it to make pipes or hair fatter in some spots and thinner in others.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Radius: Thickness at each point. 0 makes it vanish, small is thin, large is thick.

GeometryNodeSetCurveTilt.node: Twists the curve around its own direction at each point. Use it to roll ribbons or profile shapes along a path.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Tilt: The twist angle in degrees. 0 is no twist, larger angles roll it more, and a full turn returns to the start.

GeometryNodeSetGeometryBundle.node: Attaches a bundle (a packed group of values) to a geometry. Use it to carry extra data along with the geometry.

inputs.Bundle: The group of values to attach to the geometry.

GeometryNodeSetGeometryName.node: Gives a geometry a name. It helps you tell pieces apart when debugging, and it does not change how it looks.

inputs.Name: The text name to give the geometry.

GeometryNodeSetGreasePencilColor.node: Sets the color and see-through level of Grease Pencil strokes or fills. Use it to recolor a drawing.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Color: The color to apply to the strokes.
inputs.Opacity: How solid the color is. 0 is fully invisible, 1 is fully solid.

GeometryNodeSetGreasePencilDepth.node: Chooses how Grease Pencil strokes are layered in depth: by 2D order or by 3D position. Use it to fix strokes that overlap wrongly.

GeometryNodeSetGreasePencilSoftness.node: Sets how soft the edges of Grease Pencil strokes are. Use it for a blurry or crisp look.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Softness: How fuzzy the stroke edge is. 0 is crisp and sharp, 1 is very soft and blurry.

GeometryNodeSetGridBackground.node: Sets the value used for empty cells in a volume grid. Use it to define what 'nothing' means outside the active area.

inputs.Background: The value for empty space. For a density grid, 0 means no fog out there.
inputs.Update Inactive: When on, existing empty cells are updated to the new background. When off, they keep their old values.

GeometryNodeSetGridTransform.node: Changes how a volume grid sits in space (its position, rotation and size). Use it to move or scale a whole grid.

inputs.Transform: The matrix that places the grid into the object's space. The identity matrix means no change.

GeometryNodeSetID.node: Sets the ID number on each element. Used for random effects and keeping things steady over time.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.ID: The number to store. Elements with different IDs get different random results in some nodes.

GeometryNodeSetInstanceTransform.node: Sets the full placement (move, turn, size) of every instance at once with a matrix. Use it for exact control of copies.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Transform: The matrix that decides where each instance sits, how it is turned and how big it is.

GeometryNodeSetMaterial.node: Gives a material to the selected faces or elements. Use it to color or texture parts of a shape.

inputs.Selection: Picks which faces get the material. True means assigned, false means left alone.
inputs.Material: The material to apply to the selected parts.

GeometryNodeSetMaterialIndex.node: Changes which material slot number each face uses. Use it to switch a face from one slot's material to another.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Material Index: The slot number. 0 is the first slot, 1 the second, and so on.

GeometryNodeSetMeshNormal.node: Stores custom normals (shading directions) or sharpness on a mesh. Use it to control how light and shadow look across faces.

inputs.Remove Custom: When on, clears custom normals and goes back to ones computed automatically.
inputs.Edge Sharpness: When on, the edge sharpness marks decide where shading breaks. When off, edges blend smoothly.
inputs.Face Sharpness: When on, the face smooth setting decides if faces look flat or smooth. When off, faces follow the other normals.

GeometryNodeSetNURBSOrder.node: Changes how many control points influence each part of a NURBS curve. Use it to make the curve stiffer or looser.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Order: Low (2) follows the control points closely like straight lines. Higher values (up to 6) give smoother, rounder curves.

GeometryNodeSetNURBSWeight.node: Changes how strongly each NURBS control point pulls the curve. Use it to bend a curve closer to or away from points.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Weight: Pull strength of the point. 1 is normal, higher pulls the curve nearer, lower lets it move away.

GeometryNodeSetPointRadius.node: Sets the size of points in a point cloud. Use it to make dots bigger or smaller.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Radius: Size of each point. Small gives tiny dots, large gives big balls.

GeometryNodeSetPosition.node: Moves points to a new place, or pushes them by an offset. Use it to bend, wiggle or reshape geometry.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Position: The new location of each point. By default it keeps its current place.
inputs.Offset: An extra move added to the position. Zero keeps points still, larger values push them further.

GeometryNodeSetShadeSmooth.node: Makes faces look smooth or flat in shading, without changing the shape. Use it to fix a faceted look on round objects.

inputs.Selection: Picks which faces change shading. True means changed, false means left alone.
inputs.Shade Smooth: On makes faces look smooth and blended. Off makes each face look flat and edgy.

GeometryNodeSetSplineCyclic.node: Opens or closes curves into loops. Use it to join the ends of a curve or cut a loop open.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Cyclic: On connects the end back to the start to make a loop. Off leaves the curve open.

GeometryNodeSetSplineResolution.node: Sets how many points are made along each curve segment when drawn. Use it for smoother or lighter curves.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Resolution: Low gives rough, angular curves. High gives smooth curves but costs more memory.

GeometryNodeSimulationInput.node: Starts a simulation zone, where the result of each frame feeds the next one. Use it for things that change over time, like falling or growing.

GeometryNodeSimulationOutput.node: Ends a simulation zone and passes out the result of the current frame. Use it to store state over time.

inputs.Skip: When on, the simulation pauses and skips this frame's update. When off, it runs normally.

GeometryNodeSortElements.node: Reorders elements by a weight number, which changes their index. Use it to control which element comes first, second, and so on.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Group ID: Elements are sorted separately inside each group number.
inputs.Sort Weight: Lower weights come first, higher weights come last.

GeometryNodeSortList.node: Reorders a list of values based on weights. Use it to put list items in a chosen order.

inputs.List: The list of values to sort.
inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Group ID: Items are sorted separately inside each group number.
inputs.Sort Weight: Lower weights come first, higher weights come last.

GeometryNodeSplineLength.node: Gives each curve's total length, and the number of points on it. Use it to size things to fit a curve.

GeometryNodeSplineParameter.node: Tells how far along its curve each point is: as a factor from 0 to 1, as a length, and as an index. Use it to grade effects along a path.

GeometryNodeSplitEdges.node: Separates faces by splitting the edges between them. Use it to make hard breaks, like cut seams or a low-poly look.

inputs.Selection: Picks which edges are split apart. True means split, false means kept joined.

GeometryNodeSplitToInstances.node: Turns each group of elements into its own instance. Use it to treat chunks of a mesh as separate pieces.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Group ID: Elements with the same number go in the same piece. Different numbers become different pieces.

GeometryNodeStoreNamedAttribute.node: Saves a value as an attribute with a name you pick. Use it to pass data to materials or later nodes.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Name: The name for the stored attribute. Use the same name later to read it back.
inputs.Value: The data to save on each element. It can be a number, vector, color and so on.

GeometryNodeStoreNamedGrid.node: Saves a volume grid under a name inside volume geometry. Use it to keep several grids together in one volume.

inputs.Name: The name to save the grid under. Use it later to find the grid again.

GeometryNodeStringJoin.node: Glues several text strings into one, with a separator between them. Use it to build labels or names.

inputs.Delimiter: Text placed between each string, like a comma or space. Empty means they are stuck right together.
inputs.Strings: The pieces of text to join, in order.

GeometryNodeStringToCurves.node: Turns text into 3D letter shapes made of curves. Use it for titles and signs.

inputs.String: The text to turn into shapes.
inputs.Size: How tall the letters are. Small is tiny text, large is big text.
inputs.Font: The font that gives the letters their look.
inputs.Align X: How text lines up sideways: left, center, right, justified or flush.
inputs.Align Y: How text lines up up and down: top, middle, bottom and similar.
inputs.Pivot Point: The point the whole text block is positioned around, such as top left or center.
inputs.Character Spacing: Space between letters. Less than 1 packs them tight, more than 1 spreads them out.
inputs.Word Spacing: Space between words. Less than 1 brings words close, more than 1 pushes them apart.
inputs.Line Spacing: Space between lines. Less than 1 stacks lines tight, more than 1 spreads them out.
inputs.Overflow: What happens when text does not fit the box: let it overflow, scale it to fit, or cut it off.
inputs.Text Box Width: Width of the box that holds the text. 0 means no limit, small values wrap text onto more lines.
inputs.Text Box Height: Height of the box that holds the text. 0 means no limit, small values cut or shrink long text.

GeometryNodeSubdivideCurve.node: Splits each curve segment into smaller pieces by adding points. Use it to get more points to bend or move.

inputs.Cuts: How many new points are added in each segment. 0 does nothing, higher gives more detail.

GeometryNodeSubdivideMesh.node: Splits faces into smaller ones without smoothing the shape. Use it to add more points to a mesh before bending or displacing.

inputs.Level: How many times faces are split. Each level makes about 4 times more faces, so high values get heavy fast.

GeometryNodeSubdivisionSurface.node: Splits a mesh into many faces and rounds it into a smooth shape. Use it to turn a blocky model into a smooth one.

inputs.Level: How smooth it gets. 0 changes nothing. Each level adds many more faces, so high values are slow.
inputs.Edge Crease: Keeps chosen edges sharp. 0 lets them round off, 1 keeps them fully sharp.
inputs.Vertex Crease: Keeps chosen corner points sharp. 0 lets them round off, 1 keeps them fully sharp.
inputs.Limit Surface: When on, points are moved to the final smooth surface. When off, they are placed in a quicker way.
inputs.Quality: Accuracy of the smoothing on the GPU or CPU. Low is faster but rough. High is slower but more exact.
inputs.UV Smooth: Decides how UV maps are smoothed, so textures do not stretch or warp at borders.
inputs.Boundary Smooth: Decides how open borders of the mesh are smoothed. All smooths them, Keep Corners keeps corner points fixed.

GeometryNodeSwitch.node: Chooses between two inputs with a true or false switch. Use it to turn parts of your setup on and off.

inputs.Switch: False passes the False input, True passes the True input.
inputs.False: The value that goes out when the switch is off.
inputs.True: The value that goes out when the switch is on.

GeometryNodeTagFilter.node: Checks if a filter text matches a list of tags. Use it to pick items by labels, like in simulation setups.

inputs.Tag Filter: The text pattern to test, where * can stand for any text.
inputs.Tags: The list of tags to check against the filter.

GeometryNodeTool3DCursor.node: Gives the location and rotation of the 3D cursor. Use it in tools to act where the cursor is placed.

GeometryNodeToolActiveElement.node: Gives the index of the active (last clicked) element in Edit mode. Use it in tools to act on that element.

GeometryNodeToolFaceSet.node: Gives each face's sculpt face set number. Use it in tools to work with sculpt face groups.

GeometryNodeToolMousePosition.node: Gives where the mouse pointer is in the viewport. Use it in tools to react to the cursor.

GeometryNodeToolSelection.node: Gives true for the elements the user has selected in Edit mode. Use it in tools to affect only the selection.

GeometryNodeToolSetFaceSet.node: Writes sculpt face set numbers onto faces. Use it in tools to create or change face groups.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Face Set: The face set number to store. Faces with the same number form a group.

GeometryNodeToolSetSelection.node: Changes which elements are selected in Edit mode. Use it in tools to select parts based on rules.

inputs.Selection: True selects the element, false deselects it.

GeometryNodeTransferAttributes.node: Copies attributes from one geometry to another using index numbers. Use it to pass data between two shapes that match in order.

inputs.Target Point ID: Index of the point in the target used to match the source.
inputs.Target Edge ID: Index of the edge in the target used to match the source.
inputs.Target Face ID: Index of the face in the target used to match the source.
inputs.Target Corner ID: Index of the face corner in the target used to match the source.
inputs.Target Curve ID: Index of the curve in the target used to match the source.
inputs.Target Instance ID: Index of the instance in the target used to match the source.
inputs.Source Point ID: Index of the point in the source that data is copied from.
inputs.Source Edge ID: Index of the edge in the source that data is copied from.
inputs.Source Face ID: Index of the face in the source that data is copied from.
inputs.Source Corner ID: Index of the face corner in the source that data is copied from.
inputs.Source Curve ID: Index of the curve in the source that data is copied from.
inputs.Source Instance ID: Index of the instance in the source that data is copied from.
inputs.Pattern Mode: Exact copies the attributes you name. Wildcard lets * match many attribute names.
inputs.Attribute Names: Which attributes to copy. In wildcard mode, * matches any text.
inputs.Exclude Names: When on, the names listed are skipped and everything else is copied.

GeometryNodeTransform.node: Moves, turns and resizes geometry. Use it to place things in the scene or to flip and stretch them.

inputs.Mode: Components lets you set move, turn and size separately. Matrix uses one combined transform.
inputs.Translation: How far to move on X, Y, Z. 0 keeps the place, bigger numbers move further.
inputs.Rotation: How much to turn around each axis. 0 means no turn.
inputs.Scale: How much to resize. 1 keeps the size, below 1 shrinks, above 1 grows, negative flips it.
inputs.Transform: One matrix that holds move, turn and size together. Used in Matrix mode.

GeometryNodeTranslateInstances.node: Moves instances without changing the geometry inside. Use it to shift or spread out copies.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Translation: How far to move on X, Y, Z. 0 keeps the place, bigger numbers move further.
inputs.Local Space: On moves along each instance's own axes. Off moves along the world axes.

GeometryNodeTriangulate.node: Splits all faces into triangles. Use it before exporting, or to get a predictable face shape.

inputs.Selection: Picks which faces are split into triangles. Unselected faces stay as they are.
inputs.Quad Method: How a four-sided face is cut into two triangles. It changes which diagonal is used and how the shading looks.
inputs.N-gon Method: How faces with five or more sides are cut into triangles. Beauty makes even triangles, Clip works from the edge.

GeometryNodeTrimCurve.node: Cuts off parts of curves at the start or end. Use it to grow or shrink a line, like drawing it on.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Start: Where the curve begins, from 0 (original start) to 1 (original end). Raising it cuts more from the start.
inputs.End: Where the curve ends, from 0 to 1. Lowering it cuts more from the end.
inputs.Start_001: Where the curve begins, as a distance along its length. Raising it cuts more from the start.
inputs.End_001: Where the curve ends, as a distance along its length. Lowering it cuts more from the end.

GeometryNodeUVPackIslands.node: Arranges UV islands (pieces of the flat map) to fill the UV square. Use it to use texture space well and avoid overlap.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Margin: Gap between islands. 0 packs them touching, higher leaves space so textures do not bleed.
inputs.Rotate: When on, islands may be turned to fit tighter. When off, they keep their rotation.
inputs.Method: How the islands are fitted together. It decides whether packing is by shape or by bounding box.
inputs.Bottom Left: Corner of the area where packing starts. Usually (0, 0).
inputs.Top Right: Opposite corner of the packing area. Usually (1, 1).

GeometryNodeUVTangent.node: Gives the direction of the texture's U axis on the surface. Use it for normal maps and hair-like effects.

inputs.Method: Chooses how the tangent is calculated, from the UV map or from a given direction.
inputs.UV: The UV coordinates used to find the direction.

GeometryNodeUVUnwrap.node: Flattens a 3D mesh into a 2D UV map, cutting along seams. Use it to prepare a model for textures.

inputs.Selection: Picks which elements this node changes. True means changed, false means skipped. Leave it on to affect everything.
inputs.Seam: Marks the edges where the mesh is cut open when flattening.
inputs.Margin: Gap between flattened pieces. 0 lets them touch, higher leaves space between them.
inputs.Fill Holes: When on, holes in the flattened map are closed to reduce stretching. When off, they stay open.
inputs.Method: Angle Based keeps shapes natural. Conformal keeps angles better but can stretch sizes.
inputs.Iterations: How many times it refines the result. Low is quicker but can be rough, high is more even but slower.
inputs.No Flip: When on, it stops pieces from folding over themselves. Off can allow flipped faces.

GeometryNodeVertexOfCorner.node: Gives which vertex a face corner belongs to. Use it to go from a corner to the point it sits on.

inputs.Corner Index: The number of the corner to check. By default it is each corner itself.

GeometryNodeViewer.node: Shows the data plugged into it in the Spreadsheet and the viewport. Use it to peek at values while building.

GeometryNodeViewportTransform.node: Gives the position and direction of the 3D view you are looking through. Use it in tools to react to the camera view.

GeometryNodeVolumeCube.node: Makes a box of volume where a field decides the density at each spot. Use it to make fog, clouds or noise in 3D.

inputs.Density: How thick the fog is at each spot. 0 is empty, higher is thicker and darker.
inputs.Background: The value for empty space outside the active area. Usually 0.
inputs.Min: One corner of the box in space. Set the smaller X, Y, Z here.
inputs.Max: The opposite corner of the box in space. Set the larger X, Y, Z here.
inputs.Resolution X: How many cells across X. Low is rough and fast, high is detailed and slow.
inputs.Resolution Y: How many cells across Y. Low is rough and fast, high is detailed and slow.
inputs.Resolution Z: How many cells across Z. Low is rough and fast, high is detailed and slow.

GeometryNodeVolumeToMesh.node: Turns a volume or a signed distance field into a solid mesh surface. Use it to get a real model from clouds or blobs.

inputs.Resolution Mode: Grid uses the volume's own cells. Amount sets the cell count. Size sets an exact cell size.
inputs.Voxel Size: Cell size in Size mode. Small gives a detailed mesh but is heavy. Large is rough and fast.
inputs.Voxel Amount: Number of cells across the object in Amount mode. Low is rough, high is detailed and slow.
inputs.Threshold: Density value where the surface appears. Low makes a fatter shape, high makes a thinner shape.
inputs.Adaptivity: How much flat areas are simplified. 0 keeps every face, higher merges them for fewer faces.

GeometryNodeWarning.node: Shows a custom warning message on the node group. Use it to tell users when something is set up wrong.

inputs.Show: When on, the warning appears. When off, it stays hidden.
inputs.Message: The text of the warning shown to the user.

GeometryNodeXPBDSolver.node: Runs a physics simulation using the XPBD method, which moves bodies and constraints step by step. Use it for simple physics in nodes.

inputs.World: The group of data that describes the simulated world, its bodies and constraints.
inputs.Delta Time: How much time passes each step. Small is slower and more accurate, large is faster but less stable.
inputs.Filter: Text filter that chooses which parts of the world take part in the simulation.
inputs.Simulation to World: Matrix that moves the simulation space into the world space.
inputs.Substeps: How many small steps each frame is split into. More is more stable but slower.
inputs.Constraint Iterations: How many times constraints are solved per step. More makes joints stiffer and more exact but slower.
inputs.Solver Path: Where in the world data the solver looks for the things it simulates.
inputs.Begin: The time when the simulation starts.
inputs.End: The time when the simulation stops.
